Dawson IEEE-754 synthesizable floating point arithmetic cores
https://github.com/dawsonjon/fpu
Upstream commit c45d5e0a9f1b7e945e2be6770dbc1203825a05c4
Files: double_adder/double_adder.v, double_multiplier/double_multiplier.v,
double_divider/double_divider.v. These files are unmodified. 2013-2014 source;
not evidence of timing, gate count or process availability in the 1990s.
Copyright and license are reproduced in COPYING.txt.

double_adder_fast.v is a BMSX derivative of double_adder.v, retaining the MIT
license. The ALIGN stage uses a parallel shift with sticky jam instead of a
single shift per clock. Leading-zero detection and a barrel shift replace
serial left normalization while retaining guard, round and sticky. Exact
opposite-value cancellation takes the +0 path under round-to-nearest/ties-even.
The parallel leading-zero/shift organisation was compared with Berkeley
HardFloat's `AddRecFN` implementation:
https://github.com/ucb-bar/berkeley-hardfloat/blob/master/hardfloat/src/main/scala/AddRecFN.scala
The original Dawson file remains unmodified. The derivative has directed
comparisons but is not a qualified arithmetic macro.

double_divider_corrected.v is a minimally corrected serial derivative. The
rounding-overflow comparison uses all 53 significand bits instead of the
upstream 24-bit literal. The unchanged upstream returns 0020000001000000 for
0000000002000000 / 4000000000000001; the binary64 result is 0000000001000000.
The CPU/GEO service therefore uses the corrected derivative by default; the
original remains only as an explicitly characterized historical reference.

double_multiplier_fast.v and double_divider_fast.v are separate derivatives
under the same MIT license. Both use a parallel leading-zero tree and a
single sticky-jam underflow shift. The divider preloads the 52 initial radix-2
steps whose quotient is necessarily zero, and then computes one quotient bit
per clock for 56 iterations; it also retains the corrected rounding comparison.
These are bounded-work candidate datapaths, not qualified area or clock timing.
The separation of IEEE classifications, significand division and rounded
output was also checked against Berkeley HardFloat's DivSqrtRecFN_small:
https://github.com/ucb-bar/berkeley-hardfloat/blob/master/hardfloat/src/main/scala/DivSqrtRecFN_small.scala
